rationale: B wins by editorial restraint. Its "Perplexity now earns a fee when you buy what it recommends" finds a clean user-trust story A missed, while A's cleverest swing, "Perplexity is now paid twice on the same answer," is an inference wearing a headline. A has better proof demands, but it also opens with "publishers it was being sued over," and the source only says criticism and legal threats; that is how you invite a correction before you get a clip.
gaps_in_A: "Perplexity starts paying publishers it was being sued over" overstates legal threats into actual lawsuits; the update does not say Perplexity was sued.
"those same publishers" implies the publishers that threatened action are the payout recipients or enrolled; no participating publisher is named.
"Perplexity is now paid twice on the same answer" is only true if referral revenue sits outside the shared pool; the set admits this but still headlines it as fact.

"A multi-billion-dollar valuation now has two revenue lines to defend it" is thin without revenue figures or investor quotes; the set knows it, but it is still padding compared with the stronger angles.
gaps_in_B: "The launch is the first concrete monetization signal since the raise" invents sequence; the update says recent raise and new revenue lines, not first signal.
"takes a referral fee on every sale" may overstate the commercial terms; the facts only say Perplexity earns a referral fee from in-app purchases.
It rejects "Hundreds of millions of queries a month" too quickly; with citation rate, ad inventory, and share percentage, that can be a valid media-economics angle.
"Four viable shapes exist" is too confident until payout, merchant, and disclosure terms are answerable; the publisher and VC angles can collapse without numbers.
